subdomain: 1.2 Design end-to-end architectures (input → processing → output → feedback loops)

en.question: A self-hosted Agent SDK application produces spreadsheets in each session's working directory. Session transcripts are mirrored to durable storage, but working directories are ephemeral. After a container is rescheduled, the resumed agent refers to files that no longer exist. Which architecture change addresses the actual state gap?

options.text: Increase the transcript retention period and resume each session from its latest mirrored conversation turn.
options.note: Retaining conversation records longer does not persist files outside those records. The agent can remember a file path while the referenced artifact remains absent.

options.text: Recreate the working directory by asking Claude to infer each file's contents from its prior completion messages.
options.note: Completion messages need not contain complete, exact file data. Regeneration from descriptions cannot establish recovery of the original artifacts.

options.text: Keep the container stateless and disable resumption so users restart any interrupted artifact-producing task.
options.note: Restarting avoids a misleading resume but sacrifices the stated session continuity and can repeat costly work. It does not solve durable artifact recovery.

options.text: Persist workspace artifacts independently, preserving their session association, and restore them together with the conversation state.
options.note: The self-hosted subprocess has both transcript state and filesystem state. Recovering both, with the correct session mapping, restores the artifacts referenced by the resumed conversation.
